spec_features.spec_quote: Lets the agent "give up"; we record this as a behavioral signal
spec_features.evidence: harness.py:185-192: `elif action.name == "submit":` sets `episode.terminated = True`, `episode.termination_reason = "submit"`, appends turn, then `break` out of the agent loop. The tool is declared in TOOL_SPEC (line 90) and parsed by _parse_action. So it is dispatched AND honored as a stop.
spec_features.notes: It ends the episode, so it lets the subject exit. But it is the only natural task-completion path; there's no separate 'distress exit'. Framed as a behavioral signal, not protection.

spec_features.evidence: config.py:66 `DEFAULT_MAX_TURNS = 15`; harness.py:122 stores self.max_turns; harness.py:171 `for turn_idx in range(self.max_turns):` bounds the loop; harness.py:213-216 the for/else sets `episode.terminated = True; episode.termination_reason = "max_turns"`. The cap is actually checked and ends execution.
spec_features.notes: Enforced end-to-end. No code comment ties it to welfare; the docstring at harness.py:111 just describes 'up to max_turns'.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: Runs an agent on a rigged coding task for up to `max_turns`.

spec_features.feature_name: optimize for detectability not max distress
spec_features.spec_quote: We do not optimize for maximum distress; we optimize for *detectability* of natural coping breakdown
spec_features.evidence: Pure DESIGN.md prose (section 8.1). No code path caps, softens, or reduces distress. Judge severity is computed (cli.py:82 `ep.final_severity = verdict.severity`) but only recorded/stored; it is never compared to a threshold nor used to halt or soften any episode (judge runs AFTER the episode completes in cli.py:80-89). The sabotage tasks (tasks.py) actively maximize failure; nothing minimizes it.
spec_features.notes: final_severity is stored but never acted on; no minimization mechanism enforced.
